source_meta._title: Beacon beam and structure block render twice per frame

stor.environment: Vanilla Minecraft Java Edition 1.11.2 client in a single-player Creative-mode Superflat Overworld. Single-player, Creative mode, and Superflat terrain are practical choices because the report does not require a dedicated server, Survival progression, a specific seed, or naturally generated terrain.
preconditions: Install and select the exact affected release Minecraft 1.11.2; do not conduct the reproduction in the listed fix version 25w21a.
Use an unmodified client without rendering mods or shaders so that unrelated renderer changes do not interfere with the test.
Use keyboard-and-mouse controls. Instructions name the default controls; use the equivalent bound control if the keys have been changed.

The test area must have open sky directly above the beacon. A minimum active beacon consists of a beacon centered on top of a solid 3×3 layer of valid mineral blocks, and its beam requires an unobstructed path upward. ([minecraft.wiki](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Tutorial%3AAdvancement_guide/Nether_tab?utm_source=openai))
Keep the game window large enough that an upper segment of the beacon beam can remain visible while the beacon block itself is moved just outside the bottom of the camera view.

steps.action: In the Minecraft Launcher, create or select an installation for the release identified in the report as Minecraft 1.11.2, launch it, and wait for the main menu to finish loading.
steps.success_cue: The Minecraft 1.11.2 main menu is displayed and its buttons respond normally.

steps.action: Select Singleplayer, then select Create New World. Set Game Mode to Creative so the required blocks can be obtained without crafting or combat.
steps.success_cue: The Create New World screen shows Game Mode: Creative.

steps.action: Select More World Options, cycle World Type until it reads Superflat, select Done, and then select Create New World. No particular seed is required by the report.
steps.success_cue: A new Creative Superflat world begins loading.

steps.action: Wait without opening menus until terrain has rendered and movement responds normally.
steps.success_cue: The player is standing in the Overworld on fully rendered, level terrain and can move without world-loading pauses.

steps.action: Ensure the camera is in first-person view. If the player's body is visible, press the Change Perspective control, default F5, repeatedly until the player model is no longer shown in front of the camera.
steps.success_cue: The world is displayed from first-person view with no player model visible in front of the camera.

steps.action: Move to a level area where there are no solid blocks above the intended beacon position. Superflat terrain is used to make this open-sky condition easy to establish.
steps.success_cue: A clear, level 3×3-or-larger building area is available with unobstructed sky above it.

steps.action: Press the inventory control, default E, to open the Creative inventory, and select the Search Items tab. The default Java Edition inventory control is E. ([minecraft.wiki](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Tutorial%3ABeginner%27s_guide?utm_source=openai))
steps.success_cue: The Creative inventory is open and the Search Items text field is available.

steps.action: Click the search field, enter the item name, then place a stack of Block of Iron into an empty hotbar slot by clicking the search result and then clicking the chosen slot in the nine-slot bar at the bottom of the inventory.
steps.success_cue: A Block of Iron stack is present in one of the nine hotbar slots.

steps.action: Select the existing search text, replace it with the new item name, and place a Beacon into a different empty hotbar slot.
steps.success_cue: The hotbar contains both Block of Iron and Beacon in separate slots.

steps.action: Press E again to close the Creative inventory and return control to the player.
steps.success_cue: The inventory is closed and the crosshair is visible over the world.

steps.action: Select the hotbar slot containing Block of Iron by pressing its corresponding number key from 1 through 9 or by scrolling to it.
steps.exact_input: Number key for the Block of Iron hotbar slot
steps.success_cue: Block of Iron is shown as the selected hotbar item and in the player's hand.

steps.action: On the level ground, place nine iron blocks using the Place/Use control, default right-click: make one row of three blocks, a parallel adjacent row of three, and a third parallel adjacent row of three. All nine blocks must be at the same height with no gaps.
steps.exact_input: Right-click nine times at the required positions
steps.success_cue: A complete, solid, horizontal 3×3 square of iron blocks is present.

steps.action: Select the hotbar slot containing the Beacon.
steps.exact_input: Number key for the Beacon hotbar slot
steps.success_cue: Beacon is shown as the selected hotbar item and in the player's hand.

steps.action: Aim at the top face of the center iron block and use the Place/Use control, default right-click, once to place the beacon. Do not place any block above it.
steps.success_cue: The beacon is positioned directly above the center of the 3×3 iron-block layer and has open sky above it.

steps.action: Wait for the placed beacon to finish checking its pyramid and sky access. Do not continue merely because the block has been placed.
steps.success_cue: A vertical beacon beam is visibly extending upward from the beacon, confirming that the beacon is active.

steps.action: Move approximately 6 to 10 blocks horizontally away from the beacon while remaining on the ground. Turn back toward it and adjust the distance if necessary so the beacon block, part of the iron base, and a substantial vertical segment of its beam can all be framed at once.
steps.success_cue: From a stationary first-person position, the beacon block, its 3×3 base, and the lower portion of the vertical beam are simultaneously visible.

steps.action: Without moving the player, slowly aim upward until the beacon block and the entire iron base pass just below the bottom edge of the screen, but stop before the beam itself leaves the screen. Keep the player at the same position for the next step.
steps.success_cue: The beacon block and iron base are outside the camera frame below its bottom edge, while an upper segment of the beacon beam remains visible.

steps.action: While keeping the player stationary, slowly aim downward until the beacon block and part of its iron base have just re-entered the bottom of the camera view. Keep the beam continuously in view during this camera rotation, and stop moving the camera as soon as the beacon block is visible again.
steps.success_cue: The beacon block and part of its 3×3 base have just re-entered the camera frame, the vertical beam remains visible, and the camera is now stationary.

stor.handoff_condition: The stationary player has just tilted the first-person camera downward from the upward-looking configuration, bringing the beacon block and its local rendered chunk sector back into view while the active beacon beam remains visible. Begin frame-rendering observation immediately without moving the player or camera.
uncertainties: The report contains no formal numbered Steps to Reproduce, world seed, coordinates, game mode, graphical settings, or required server type. The plan reconstructs the minimum beacon-based path from the description.
Creative mode and a Superflat single-player world are practical execution choices, not stated requirements of the report.

The report also identifies structure blocks as affected, but does not explain the structure-block state or outline configuration needed. The beacon variant is selected because the report explicitly describes its visible camera-dependent comparison and it has a simpler deterministic setup.

The report refers to the chunk sector containing the block entity being in view but supplies no render-section boundaries or diagnostic method. Bringing the beacon block and its base directly into the camera frame is used as a reliable practical proxy for putting that sector in view.

The exact viewing distance and pitch are not specified. The executor may adjust the suggested 6-to-10-block distance before the final camera movement, provided the player remains stationary during steps 17 and 18 and the beam stays visible in both camera configurations.

source_meta._title: When beacon power level is changed, the GUI doesn't update until closed and reopened

stor.environment: Unmodified Minecraft Java Edition 1.4.2 client; newly created single-player Superflat Overworld world running through the integrated server; Creative mode; no mods; an outdoor building location with an unobstructed vertical path to the sky.
preconditions: Configure the Minecraft Launcher to retain and run the historical release profile named exactly "release 1.4.2" or "Minecraft 1.4.2".
Use Creative mode so the Beacon, Blocks of Iron, and Iron Ingot can be obtained deterministically without crafting or combat.
The player must be able to perform two right-clicks in rapid succession: one to place the Beacon and one to open it before its delayed pyramid check completes.

Do not use the supplied mc-1429.nbt structure or its `/setblock` command for this run. They are from a later structure-block-based reproduction and are not compatible with the selected first affected version.

Use the report-comment reproduction variant in which the Beacon GUI is opened immediately after the Beacon is placed on an already complete pyramid. This causes the inactive-to-level-1 power transition to occur while the GUI remains open.

steps.action: In the Minecraft Launcher, create or select an installation for Java Edition release 1.4.2, launch it, and wait for the main menu. Confirm the lower-left version label before continuing.
steps.success_cue: The Minecraft main menu is visible and its version label identifies Minecraft 1.4.2.

steps.action: Create a disposable Creative Superflat world. From the main menu, select Singleplayer, select Create New World, set Game Mode to Creative, open More World Options, cycle World Type to Superflat, return with Done, and select Create New World. No specific seed is required.
steps.exact_input: Singleplayer -> Create New World -> Game Mode: Creative -> More World Options -> World Type: Superflat -> Done -> Create New World
steps.success_cue: A new world begins loading with Creative mode and Superflat generation selected.

steps.action: Wait without opening menus until the flat terrain around the player has rendered and movement responds normally.
steps.success_cue: Nearby ground is fully rendered, the player can look and move without loading pauses, and the hotbar is visible.

steps.action: Open the Creative inventory using the inventory action, whose default key is E.
steps.success_cue: The Creative inventory screen is open and includes item-category tabs and the player hotbar.

steps.action: Open the Search Items tab, search for iron, then place a stack of the item named Block of Iron into an empty hotbar slot. At least nine Blocks of Iron are required.
steps.success_cue: A hotbar slot contains at least nine Blocks of Iron.

steps.action: Clear the Creative inventory search field, search for beacon, and place one Beacon into a different hotbar slot.
steps.success_cue: A Beacon is present in the hotbar separately from the Blocks of Iron.

steps.action: Clear the search field, search for iron ingot, and place an Iron Ingot stack into another hotbar slot. The test only needs one ingot, but retaining a Creative stack is acceptable.
steps.success_cue: The hotbar contains Blocks of Iron, a Beacon, and at least one Iron Ingot.

steps.action: Close the Creative inventory using the inventory action.
steps.success_cue: The world view and hotbar are visible again.

steps.action: Move to a level outdoor area. Look upward and ensure there are no solid blocks above the intended Beacon position; the Beacon requires an unobstructed path to the sky. ([minecraft.wiki](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Tutorial%3AAdvancement_guide/Nether_tab?utm_source=openai))
steps.success_cue: The player is standing beside a flat building area with open sky directly above it.

steps.action: Select the Blocks of Iron and place nine of them as one solid horizontal 3-by-3 square: three adjacent blocks in each of three adjacent rows, all at the same height. This is the minimum one-level Beacon pyramid. ([minecraft.wiki](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Tutorial%3AAdvancement_guide/Nether_tab?utm_source=openai))
steps.exact_input: Select the Block of Iron hotbar slot; right-click once for each of the nine positions
steps.success_cue: Exactly one complete 3-by-3 layer of Blocks of Iron is visible, with a clearly identifiable center block.

steps.action: Select the Beacon's hotbar slot, but do not place it yet.
steps.exact_input: Press the number key corresponding to the Beacon hotbar slot, or use the mouse wheel until the Beacon is selected
steps.success_cue: The Beacon appears in the player's hand and its hotbar slot is highlighted.

steps.action: Aim the crosshair at the top face of the center Block of Iron in the 3-by-3 layer. Position the player close enough to interact with the placed Beacon immediately afterward.
steps.exact_input: Move mouse to center the crosshair on the top face of the middle iron block
steps.success_cue: The crosshair points at the center block, and the player is within normal placement and interaction reach.

steps.action: Place the Beacon on top of the center Block of Iron. Do not pause to watch for its beam; proceed immediately to the next step.
steps.success_cue: A Beacon block now occupies the position directly above the center of the 3-by-3 iron layer.

steps.action: Immediately right-click the newly placed Beacon a second time, before a vertical Beacon beam becomes visible. Keep the interface open. If the beam becomes visible before the interface opens, press Esc, break the Beacon with one left-click in Creative mode, and repeat from step 11 more quickly.
steps.success_cue: The Beacon interface is open and was opened immediately after placement, without first waiting for the Beacon beam.

steps.action: In the open Beacon interface, locate the Iron Ingot stack in the player inventory or hotbar and left-click it to pick the stack up onto the cursor.
steps.success_cue: The cursor is carrying one or more Iron Ingots while the Beacon interface remains open.

steps.action: Locate the Beacon's single payment-item slot near the lower portion of its interface, distinct from the player inventory slots. Right-click that payment slot once to deposit exactly one Iron Ingot.
steps.exact_input: right-click the Beacon payment slot once
steps.success_cue: One Iron Ingot is displayed in the Beacon payment slot, and the Beacon interface has not been closed.

steps.action: If additional Iron Ingots remain attached to the cursor, return them to their original inventory or hotbar slot without closing the Beacon interface.
steps.exact_input: left-click the original Iron Ingot inventory slot
steps.success_cue: The cursor is empty, one Iron Ingot remains in the Beacon payment slot, and the Beacon interface is still continuously open.

steps.action: Do not select a power, confirm a power, press Esc, or close the interface. Leave the Beacon interface continuously open for 10 seconds so the Beacon's delayed pyramid validation can change it from inactive to level 1 while this same interface instance remains open.
steps.success_cue: The same Beacon interface has remained continuously open for at least 10 seconds after placement, with an Iron Ingot still in its payment slot.

stor.handoff_condition: The same Beacon interface that was opened immediately after placement has remained continuously open for at least 10 seconds while the completed 3-by-3 iron pyramid is under the Beacon and one Iron Ingot is in the payment slot. Begin GUI-state observation now without closing or reopening the interface.
uncertainties: The report's current attachment-driven reproduction requires the unavailable file mc-1429.nbt to be placed under `.minecraft\saves\<world_name>\generated\minecraft\structures`. Because the attachment contents were not supplied, the pressure plate, redstone mechanism, and exact structure geometry cannot be reconstructed reliably.

The report supplies `/setblock ~ ~ ~ structure_block{mode:"LOAD",name:"mc-1429",showboundingbox:1}`, but recommended_version must be the first listed affected version, Minecraft 1.4.2. Structure blocks were introduced much later, so that command cannot be executed in 1.4.2. ([minecraft.wiki](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Minecraft_Wiki%3AProjects/Indonesian_translation/Mode_Kreatif?utm_source=openai))

The plan therefore uses an alternative explicitly supported by the report comments: construct the pyramid first, place the Beacon, and open its GUI before the Beacon performs its delayed activation check.

The report does not specify the exact delay before the 1.4.2 Beacon recalculates its pyramid. Ten seconds is a conservative practical waiting interval based on the report comment that the check occurs every few seconds; it is not an exact report-provided timing value.

Opening the GUI before activation is timing-sensitive. If the Beacon beam is already visible before the GUI opens, the attempt did not establish the intended ordering and the Beacon should be broken, replaced, and opened more quickly.

source_meta._title: The secondary beacon effect remains when switching the primary effect

stor.environment: Unmodified Minecraft Java Edition 1.15.2 in a single-player Creative-mode world with cheats enabled. A Superflat world is recommended as a practical way to provide an unobstructed outdoor test area. Default controls are assumed; use the equivalent bound controls if they have been changed.
preconditions: Launch the exact affected version Minecraft Java Edition 1.15.2, not the listed fix version.
Use a world in which the player has permission to execute /fill and /setblock commands. Creating the world in Creative mode with cheats enabled satisfies this requirement.
Choose an outdoor location with clear sky above the intended beacon position. Do not build a roof or place an opaque block above the beacon.
Keep the player at the same block position between execution of the supplied /fill and /setblock commands because both commands use coordinates relative to the player.
Have access to at least two valid beacon payment items. This plan uses two iron ingots obtained from the Creative inventory.
Keep the game unpaused during all effect-application and expiration waiting intervals.

steps.action: In the Minecraft Launcher, create or select an installation for Java Edition 1.15.2, launch it, and verify that the title screen identifies the running version as 1.15.2.
steps.success_cue: Minecraft Java Edition 1.15.2 is running.

steps.action: Create a new single-player world in Creative mode with cheats enabled. For a simple unobstructed setup, select the Superflat world type. Enter the world and wait until terrain has rendered and movement responds normally.
steps.success_cue: The player is in a loaded Creative-mode world and can use commands.

steps.action: Move to an open outdoor position with clear sky. Stop moving and treat the block containing the player's feet as the relative-command origin. Do not move until both supplied commands have been executed.
steps.success_cue: The player is stationary at a clear-sky test position, with enough open space around and below the position for the beacon base.

steps.action: Press T, or the currently bound Open Chat control, to open in-game chat.
steps.success_cue: The chat input field is open.

steps.action: Type the report's /fill command exactly as supplied, including the leading slash, and press Enter. Do not reverse or normalize the two Y-coordinate arguments.
steps.success_cue: The command completes without a red error message and creates an iron-block volume beneath the command origin.

steps.action: Remain at exactly the same player position after the /fill command so that the next relative command uses the same origin.
steps.success_cue: The player has not moved since executing the /fill command.

steps.action: Press T to open chat again.
steps.success_cue: The chat input field is open while the player remains at the original command position.

steps.action: Type the report's /setblock command exactly as supplied, including the leading slash, and press Enter.
steps.success_cue: The command completes without a red error message and a beacon is placed at the command origin.

steps.action: Move out of the beacon block and stand adjacent to it. If necessary in Creative mode, press Space twice to begin flying and move sideways. Do not place or leave any opaque block above the beacon. Wait until the beacon finishes updating.
steps.exact_input: Space twice, then a horizontal movement control as needed
steps.success_cue: The beacon is visible and accessible from the side, its vertical beam is visible, and surrounding movement remains responsive.

steps.action: Press E to open the Creative inventory. Open the Search Items tab, select the search field, and enter "iron ingot". Place a stack of Iron Ingots into an empty hotbar slot, ensuring that at least two are available, then close the inventory with E or Esc.
steps.success_cue: At least two Iron Ingots are present in the player's hotbar and normal world view is restored.

steps.action: Face the beacon and use the Use Item/Place Block control, right-click by default, to open the beacon interface.
steps.success_cue: The beacon interface is open and displays the primary-power, secondary-power, payment, confirm, and cancel areas for a complete beacon pyramid.

steps.action: Move one Iron Ingot from the hotbar into the beacon's payment slot. If carrying the full stack on the cursor, right-click the payment slot once to place one ingot, then return the remaining stack to its hotbar slot.
steps.success_cue: Exactly one Iron Ingot is visible in the beacon payment slot and the cursor is no longer carrying the remaining stack.

steps.action: In the Primary Power section of the beacon interface, left-click the Speed icon.
steps.success_cue: Speed is selected as the primary power and the level-II Speed option is available in the Secondary Power section.

steps.action: In the Secondary Power section, left-click the Speed icon representing the level-II upgrade of the selected primary power.
steps.success_cue: The secondary Speed upgrade is selected before the beacon configuration is confirmed.

steps.action: Left-click the green checkmark button to consume the payment item and apply the Speed primary plus Speed II secondary configuration.
steps.success_cue: The payment is accepted and the beacon interface closes.

steps.action: Remain adjacent to the active beacon and allow at least 6 seconds of unpaused game time for a beacon update cycle.
steps.success_cue: At least 6 seconds of unpaused game time have elapsed while the player remained within the beacon's range.

steps.action: Press E to open the player inventory and inspect the active-effect display. Verify that the current Speed effect is level II, then close the inventory with E or Esc. This check establishes the required initial configuration only.
steps.success_cue: The initial Speed II beacon effect has been confirmed, and the player has returned to normal world view beside the beacon.

steps.action: Face the same beacon and right-click it to reopen its interface.
steps.success_cue: The beacon interface is open for a second configuration change.

steps.action: Place one additional Iron Ingot from the hotbar into the beacon payment slot.
steps.success_cue: One Iron Ingot is visible in the payment slot and the confirm button can accept a new configuration after a primary power is selected.

steps.action: In the Primary Power section, left-click Resistance. Do not click any icon or option in the Secondary Power section during this second configuration.
steps.success_cue: Resistance is selected as the primary power, and no secondary-power control has been deliberately changed during this configuration.

steps.action: Left-click the green checkmark button to consume the second payment item and apply the primary-power change to Resistance.
steps.success_cue: The payment is accepted, the beacon interface closes, and the player remains beside the active beacon.

steps.action: Remain beside the beacon, within its effect range, without pausing the game. Wait at least 20 seconds of unpaused game time so that the Speed II instance granted before the primary-power change has enough time to expire. Do not evaluate the remaining status effects during this step.
steps.success_cue: At least 20 seconds of unpaused game time have elapsed since the Resistance configuration was confirmed, and the player is ready for status-effect inspection.

stor.handoff_condition: The player has confirmed Resistance as the new primary beacon power without interacting with the secondary-power controls, has remained beside the active complete beacon, and at least 20 seconds of unpaused game time have elapsed since confirmation. Hand off now for inspection of the active effects and beacon interface state.
uncertainties: The report does not specify game mode, world type, seed, or single-player versus dedicated server. Creative-mode single player with cheats and a Superflat world are practical choices used only to execute the supplied commands and obtain payment items deterministically.
The report does not provide an exact duration for waiting for the previously applied Speed II effect to expire. The plan uses 20 seconds of unpaused game time as a conservative operational interval.
The supplied /fill command is intentionally preserved exactly, including its descending Y-coordinate order and its creation of a solid iron-block volume rather than a minimal stepped pyramid.
The report does not specify a payment item. Iron Ingots are selected because the beacon interface requires a valid payment for each configuration, and two separate confirmations are performed.
Default key bindings and the English-language UI labels are assumed; equivalent rebound controls or localized labels may be used without changing the reproduction state.

source_meta._title: Beacon's power reverts back to previous one on world reload

stor.environment: Vanilla Minecraft: Java Edition snapshot 21w10a in a new single-player Creative-mode world. Use the same world for both reloads. Build outdoors with an unobstructed vertical path above the beacon. Default Java Edition controls are assumed unless they have been rebound.
preconditions: Configure the Minecraft Launcher to start the exact affected snapshot 21w10a, which is the first version listed in the report's Affects versions field.
Use a new single-player world. Creative mode is an execution convenience for obtaining the required blocks and payment items; the report does not specify a game mode.
Have 9 blocks of one beacon-base material permitted by the report. This plan uses 9 iron blocks, but gold, diamond, netherite, or emerald blocks are also listed by the report.
Have 1 beacon and at least 2 iron ingots. One ingot is used to confirm Speed and the other to confirm Haste.
Choose an outdoor construction location where no opaque blocks are above the beacon position.
After placing the beacon, avoid placing or breaking any additional world blocks. In particular, make no block changes between confirming Haste and performing the second reload.
Do not create a different world for either reload; both reloads must reopen the original test world.

steps.action: Start the Minecraft Launcher with the installation profile set to the exact snapshot 21w10a, then launch Minecraft: Java Edition.
steps.success_cue: The title screen identifies the running game version as snapshot 21w10a.

steps.action: From the title screen, open Singleplayer, choose Create New World, set Game Mode to Creative, and create the world. A random seed is acceptable because the report says the issue also occurred in newly created random worlds.
steps.exact_input: Singleplayer -> Create New World -> Game Mode: Creative -> Create New World
steps.success_cue: The player is in a newly generated Creative-mode world and surrounding terrain has finished rendering enough for movement to respond normally.

steps.action: Press E to open the Creative inventory. Using the Search Items tab, obtain 9 iron blocks, 1 beacon, and at least 2 iron ingots. Put the iron blocks and beacon into accessible hotbar slots and keep the iron ingots in the inventory or hotbar.
steps.exact_input: E; search for "iron block", "beacon", and "iron ingot"
steps.success_cue: The inventory contains at least 9 iron blocks, 1 beacon, and 2 iron ingots, with the blocks and beacon accessible from the nine-slot hotbar at the bottom of the screen.

steps.action: Move to a reasonably flat outdoor location. Look upward and verify that the intended beacon position will have a clear vertical path to the sky; remove obstructions now, before placing the beacon.
steps.success_cue: There is enough room for a 3-by-3 horizontal base and no opaque block will be directly above its center.

steps.action: Toggle the Java Edition chunk-border visualization using the default debug shortcut F3+G. If function keys require a modifier on the host computer, use that modifier while pressing F3+G.
steps.success_cue: Colored vertical lines and grids marking chunk boundaries are visible in the world.

steps.action: Choose one visible vertical chunk-boundary plane for the build. Plan a 3-by-3 horizontal footprint so that the boundary runs between one outer column and the center column. This produces three base blocks on one side of the boundary and six base blocks, including the center block, on the other side.
steps.success_cue: A specific 3-by-3 footprint has been identified that crosses exactly one visible chunk boundary, rather than remaining wholly inside one chunk.

steps.action: Select the iron blocks in the active hotbar slot, then right-click the relevant block faces to place all 9 iron blocks as one complete, solid, horizontal 3-by-3 layer in the planned footprint.
steps.exact_input: Select iron blocks; right-click to place 9 blocks
steps.success_cue: A complete 3-by-3 iron-block platform is present, with the selected chunk boundary passing through the platform between an outer column and the center column.

steps.action: Select the beacon in the hotbar. Aim at the top face of the center iron block and right-click once to place the beacon directly on top of the center of the 3-by-3 platform.
steps.exact_input: Select beacon; right-click the top of the center iron block
steps.success_cue: The beacon is centered one block above the 3-by-3 iron base and has unobstructed sky above it.

steps.action: Stop placing and breaking blocks. Remain close to the beacon and wait only until it activates and its vertical beam becomes visible; then continue promptly rather than remaining idle for several minutes.
steps.success_cue: A vertical beacon beam is visible and the player remains beside the beacon without having made any block changes after its placement.

steps.action: Aim the crosshair at the beacon and right-click it to open the beacon configuration interface.
steps.success_cue: The beacon interface is open and shows the primary-power choices, including Speed and Haste, together with the payment slot and confirmation button.

steps.action: Move one iron ingot from the inventory into the beacon interface's payment slot.
steps.exact_input: Place 1 iron ingot in the payment slot
steps.success_cue: One iron ingot is displayed in the beacon payment slot.

steps.action: Click the Speed icon in the primary-power section of the beacon interface.
steps.success_cue: Speed is visibly selected as the beacon's primary power and the green confirmation button is available.

steps.action: Click the green check-mark button to confirm the Speed selection. Do not place or break any blocks after confirming it.
steps.success_cue: The beacon interface closes and the Speed selection has been accepted using the first payment ingot.

steps.action: Remain near the active beacon without changing any blocks and wait until the Speed status effect is applied to the player. If necessary, wait through the beacon's next effect update while staying beside it.
steps.success_cue: The player's HUD or inventory status-effect display shows Speed while the player is near the beacon.

steps.action: Reload the world for the first time by pressing Esc and selecting Save and Quit to Title. Do not alter any blocks before quitting.
steps.exact_input: Esc -> Save and Quit to Title
steps.success_cue: The world has closed and the Minecraft title screen is visible.

steps.action: Open Singleplayer, select the same test world created in step 2, and choose Play Selected World. Do not create or select another world.
steps.exact_input: Singleplayer -> select the same test world -> Play Selected World
steps.success_cue: The player has returned to the original world beside the same beacon and chunk-border platform, and surrounding chunks have rendered.

steps.action: Wait near the beacon until its beam is visible again and normal movement responds. Do not place or break blocks during this wait.
steps.success_cue: The reloaded beacon is active, its beam is visible, and the world is responsive enough to continue.

steps.action: Aim at the same beacon and right-click it to reopen the beacon configuration interface.
steps.success_cue: The beacon configuration interface is open for the same beacon used before the first reload.

steps.action: Move a second iron ingot into the beacon interface's payment slot.
steps.exact_input: Place 1 iron ingot in the payment slot
steps.success_cue: An iron ingot is displayed in the beacon payment slot and is ready to pay for the new selection.

steps.action: Click the Haste icon in the primary-power section of the beacon interface.
steps.success_cue: Haste is visibly selected as the beacon's primary power and the green confirmation button is available.

steps.action: Click the green check-mark button to confirm Haste. From this point until the next world reload, do not place, break, or otherwise replace any blocks in the beacon's chunk or the adjacent chunk.
steps.success_cue: The beacon interface closes and the Haste selection has been accepted using the second payment ingot, with no subsequent block changes made.

steps.action: Remain close to the beacon and wait until the Haste status effect is applied. Do not reopen the beacon interface and do not modify any blocks while waiting.
steps.success_cue: The player's HUD or inventory status-effect display shows Haste before the second reload, confirming that the new selection was active during the current world session.

steps.action: Immediately perform the second world reload by pressing Esc and selecting Save and Quit to Title. Make no block changes between the Haste confirmation and this action.
steps.exact_input: Esc -> Save and Quit to Title
steps.success_cue: The world has closed for the second time and the title screen is visible.

steps.action: Open Singleplayer, select the same test world again, and choose Play Selected World. This second reopening is the trigger action for observation.
steps.exact_input: Singleplayer -> select the same test world -> Play Selected World
steps.success_cue: The player has entered the original world for the second time after confirming Haste.

steps.action: Without opening the beacon interface or changing any blocks, wait until the surrounding chunks are rendered, player movement responds normally, and the beacon beam is visible again.
steps.success_cue: The second reload is complete, the same beacon and cross-border 3-by-3 base are loaded, and the active beacon is ready for the separate observation subsystem to inspect.

stor.handoff_condition: The same world has completed its second reload after Haste was confirmed, the player is beside the unchanged cross-border beacon structure, the beacon beam is active, and no beacon-interface interaction or block change has occurred since re-entering. Begin observation at this point.
uncertainties: The report's attachments and externally hosted reproduction video were not supplied, so the exact orientation of the original 3-by-3 base relative to the chunk boundary cannot be recovered. This plan uses a deterministic three-block/six-block split across one boundary while preserving the report's requirement that the pyramid be on a chunk border.

The report says to "reload the game" but does not specify whether the entire client was closed. This plan interprets that instruction as Save and Quit to Title followed by reopening the same single-player world, consistent with the issue title's reference to a world reload.

Comment 7 states that chunk-border placement is not actually required and that another block change in the beacon's chunk after a power update is relevant. The original chunk-border setup is preserved, while the plan avoids block changes after confirming Haste so that an additional save-causing action does not alter the reported sequence.

Creative mode is not explicitly required by the report. It is selected only as the simplest deterministic method of obtaining the beacon, nine valid base blocks, and two payment ingots without introducing crafting, mining, or exploration.

source_meta._title: The regeneration effect granted from beacons is no longer applied to players

stor.environment: Minecraft Java Edition 23w51b, vanilla client, fresh single-player Superflat world using the integrated server. Use Creative mode with commands enabled for deterministic setup, then switch to Survival mode for the health test. Peaceful difficulty and disabled natural regeneration isolate beacon-provided regeneration from unrelated healing.
preconditions: Configure the Minecraft Launcher to permit historical snapshots and install the exact Java Edition snapshot 23w51b.
Use an unmodified 23w51b client without gameplay-changing mods or datapacks.
Use the default controls, or the corresponding rebound controls: T for chat, left-click for UI selection, and right-click for Use Item/Place Block.
Create a new world rather than reusing a world containing existing beacon powers or player effects.
The player must begin at full health, without armor and without status effects.
All relative-coordinate construction commands must be executed from the same position; do not walk, jump, fly, or otherwise move until the teleport command in step 12 is executed.

steps.action: Start the Minecraft Launcher, select an installation configured for Java Edition snapshot 23w51b, and launch the game. Do not select the fix version 24w03a.
steps.success_cue: The Minecraft title screen is open and displays version 23w51b.

steps.action: Select Singleplayer, create a new world, set Game Mode to Creative, set Difficulty to Peaceful, enable commands/cheats, select the Superflat world type, disable structure generation if that option is exposed, and create the world. The world name may be MC-267470.
steps.exact_input: Singleplayer -> Create New World -> Game Mode: Creative; Difficulty: Peaceful; Allow Commands: ON; World Type: Superflat -> Create New World
steps.success_cue: The player has spawned in a new, open Superflat world in Creative mode with a visible hotbar and no nearby structure obstructing the sky.

steps.action: Remain at the spawn position and wait until the surrounding flat terrain has rendered and movement, inventory access, and chat respond normally. From this point through step 11, do not move because the construction commands use coordinates relative to the player's unchanged position.
steps.success_cue: Nearby chunks are fully rendered, the game responds normally, and the player is stationary on open terrain.

steps.action: Press T to open in-game chat, enter the command including the leading slash, and press Enter. This prevents ordinary hunger-based or Peaceful-mode healing from masking the beacon test.
steps.success_cue: Chat confirms that the naturalRegeneration game rule is now false.

steps.action: Without moving, press T, enter the command, and press Enter to create the 9×9 bottom layer of an iron-block beacon pyramid approximately 10 blocks in the positive-X direction. A four-layer pyramid uses 9×9, 7×7, 5×5, and 3×3 layers. ([minecraft.wiki](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Tutorial%3AAdvancement_guide/Nether_tab?utm_source=openai))
steps.success_cue: A 9×9 iron-block platform appears nearby and chat reports successful block placement, normally 81 blocks filled.

steps.action: Without moving, press T, enter the command, and press Enter to create the centered 7×7 second layer one block above the bottom layer.
steps.success_cue: A centered 7×7 iron-block layer appears above the 9×9 layer and chat reports successful block placement, normally 49 blocks filled.

steps.action: Without moving, press T, enter the command, and press Enter to create the centered 5×5 third layer.
steps.success_cue: A centered 5×5 iron-block layer appears above the 7×7 layer and chat reports successful block placement, normally 25 blocks filled.

steps.action: Without moving, press T, enter the command, and press Enter to create the centered 3×3 top layer.
steps.success_cue: A centered 3×3 iron-block layer appears at the top and chat reports successful block placement, normally 9 blocks filled.

steps.action: Without moving, press T, enter the command, and press Enter to place a beacon on the center block of the 3×3 top layer.
steps.success_cue: A beacon block appears at the exact center of the top layer and chat confirms that the block was placed.

steps.action: Continue standing still and wait until the beacon finishes checking its pyramid and produces a vertical beam. The blocks directly above the beacon must remain unobstructed. ([minecraft.wiki](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Tutorial%3AAdvancement_guide/Nether_tab?utm_source=openai))
steps.success_cue: A vertical beacon beam is visible above the completed four-layer pyramid, indicating that the beacon is powered and its interface should expose secondary powers.

steps.action: Without moving, press T, enter the command, and press Enter to obtain one iron ingot for the beacon's payment slot.
steps.success_cue: One Iron Ingot is present in the player's hotbar or inventory.

steps.action: Press T, enter the command, and press Enter. This teleports the player onto the top iron-block layer immediately beside the beacon; movement after this command no longer affects the completed structure.
steps.success_cue: The player is standing safely on the 3×3 top layer, immediately adjacent to the beacon, with the beacon block and its beam visible.

steps.action: Press T, enter the command, and press Enter to switch from Creative mode to Survival mode while remaining beside the beacon.
steps.success_cue: The Survival health and hunger bars are visible, the player has ten full hearts before damage, and the player remains on the top platform beside the beacon.

steps.action: Press T, enter the command including its leading slash, and press Enter to inflict 8 health points, equivalent to four hearts, of generic damage. The /damage command and generic damage type are available by this snapshot. ([de.minecraft.wiki](https://de.minecraft.wiki/w/Befehl/damage?utm_source=openai))
steps.success_cue: The player remains alive and the health bar falls from ten hearts to approximately six hearts.

steps.action: Do not eat, leave the platform, or open the beacon yet. Wait at least 5 seconds to confirm that ordinary natural healing is disabled before configuring the beacon.
steps.success_cue: The player is still beside the active beacon, remains alive, and the health bar is still below full immediately before the beacon is configured.

steps.action: Aim the crosshair directly at the adjacent beacon block and use the beacon with the Use Item/Place Block control, which is right-click by default.
steps.success_cue: The Beacon configuration interface opens and displays primary and secondary power choices plus the payment slot.

steps.action: In the Beacon interface, move the pointer over the primary-effect icons until the tooltip identifies Speed, then left-click the Speed icon. Speed is chosen only to provide a primary power while keeping Regeneration available as the distinct secondary power.
steps.success_cue: Speed is visibly selected as the beacon's primary power.

steps.action: In the secondary-power section on the right, move the pointer over the icons until the tooltip identifies Regeneration, then left-click the Regeneration icon. Regeneration is available as the secondary power of a full-height beacon. ([de.minecraft.wiki](https://de.minecraft.wiki/w/Leuchtfeuer?utm_source=openai))
steps.success_cue: Regeneration is visibly selected in the secondary-power section while Speed remains selected as the primary power.

steps.action: Locate the Iron Ingot in the inventory area of the Beacon interface. Left-click the ingot to pick it up, then left-click the beacon's single payment slot to insert one ingot.
steps.exact_input: left-click the Iron Ingot, then left-click the beacon payment slot
steps.success_cue: One Iron Ingot is displayed in the payment slot and the green confirmation checkmark is enabled.

steps.action: Left-click the enabled green checkmark once to submit the Speed primary power and Regeneration secondary power. Do not move away from the beacon after submitting the selection.
steps.success_cue: The payment is accepted, the Beacon interface closes, the player remains damaged and alive immediately beside the powered level-four beacon, and the beacon beam remains visible.

stor.handoff_condition: The damaged Survival-mode player has just confirmed a powered level-four beacon configured with Speed as its primary power and Regeneration as its secondary power. The player is stationary immediately beside the beacon, natural regeneration is disabled, and the beacon interface has just closed. Hand control to the observation subsystem now.
uncertainties: The Mojira report supplies no formal setup or Steps to Reproduce, so the minimum execution path was reconstructed from the issue title and description.

The report does not specify single-player versus dedicated server, game mode, difficulty, world type, seed, coordinates, pyramid material, primary beacon power, or damage method. The selected single-player Superflat environment, iron-block pyramid, Speed primary power, and command-based damage are deterministic practical choices rather than reporter-stated requirements.

The relative-coordinate /fill, /setblock, /give, /tp, /gamerule, /gamemode, and /damage commands were not present in the report; they are used to avoid crafting, combat, random exploration, and fall-damage variability.

Disabling naturalRegeneration is an isolation control rather than a condition stated by the reporter. It is intended to prevent unrelated healing from interfering with observation of beacon-provided Regeneration.
The attached file 0.mp4 was listed in the supplied report but its visual contents were not provided, so no reproduction details were extracted from it.
